claims.statement: internal/tui/theme is the TUI-local theme engine (root principle 4: it imports nothing outside internal/tui, so every filesystem path is injected by cmd/yolo); it provides the 33 embedded upstream themes, resolution, system-theme generation, terminal palette detection, custom discovery, and the selection chain (config > KV > default).

The 33 upstream theme assets are embedded verbatim (//go:embed assets/*.json -> assetsFS, the strict-copy bar of spec §1); AllThemes parses them with names as the asset file stems (kebab-case preserved: catppuccin-frappe, one-dark, ...); DefaultName is 'opencode'; IsTheme is the upstream check (a non-array object with a non-array object 'theme' member).

The Engine selection store: active = config > KV 'theme' > 'opencode' and mode = KV lock > terminal luminance > 'dark'; New mirrors the upstream init (lock = theme_mode_lock, mode = lock ?? 'dark', the one-shot theme_mode cleared when unlocked only when it holds a valid mode, active = config > KV theme > 'opencode', KV loaded synchronously so the first Get is race-free); Resolve runs the startup sequence (system theme first, the palette probed exactly here exactly once per the S0 scoping rule, then custom discovery) and always returns nil; ActiveTheme is the values memo themes[active] ?? themes[KV 'theme'] ?? themes[opencode] where themesMap = builtins + customs + optional 'system' (later entries win) and themesFromRaw filters the raw custom map to IsTheme objects round-tripped to ThemeJson.

Engine mutations: Set switches active and persists to KV 'theme' (unknown name returns false leaving the KV untouched); Pin sets the mode lock and applies it; Free clears the lock + one-shot KV keys and re-resolves the mode from the cached terminal luminance (no re-probe); Apply switches the mode and persists to KV 'theme_mode' only while locked, regenerating the system theme at the new mode from the cached palette; the two-leg refresh is Reapply (250 ms leg: regenerate the system theme at the current mode from the cached palette) and RefreshCustoms (1000 ms leg: re-discover customs; on error take the catch path — active 'opencode', customs emptied since the custom set is derived state never persisted).

DetectPalette ports TerminalPalette.detect: (1) an OSC 4;0 support probe, then (2) the 16 palette + 9 special-color queries (indices 10-17,19) with per-group idle timers, a hard timeout, and an 8192->keep-last-4096 buffer cap with first-wins stored slots; the response shapes and toHex8/scaleComponent are verbatim ports of @opentui/core 0.4.5; DetectStd probes via an owned /dev/tty in raw mode (x/term) where the fd is restored and closed on exit and the pump goroutine is joined so no reader lingers, and no controlling terminal yields (TerminalColors{}, false) (no system theme, no probe, no goroutines); LegacyTmux (TMUX set && TMUX_PANE unset) double-escapes OSC and limits the special queries to 10-12, with timeouts spec-pinned to 100 ms.

ThemeDirs is the upstream directory list: the injected global config dir first, then <dir>/.yolo for every dir from cwd up to and including the filesystem root (no dedupe, later-dir-wins); Discover scans each <dir>/themes/ for *.json (dotfiles included, symlinks followed) with name = base minus .json, later dirs overriding earlier, a missing themes dir skipped but an unreadable or unparseable file a hard error, values returned RAW (the IsTheme filter is the caller's job); WatchThemeSignals forwards SIGUSR2 to refresh (the 250/1000 ms debounce lives in the engine).

ResolveTheme ports the upstream resolver (defs refs, #hex, transparent/none, ANSI ints, and {dark,light} variants; optional selectedListItemText default background, backgroundMenu default backgroundElement, thinkingOpacity default 0.6; circular- and missing-reference errors keep the upstream wording); Rgba is stored as 0-255 uint8 (upstream RGBA is float 0-1 but every color is int-derived or float ops on 0-255 rounded at the end, so uint8 is exact and the operation order is preserved for bit-identical results); GenerateSystem turns the terminal palette + default fg/bg into a generated ThemeJson (values are Rgba mirroring upstream's RGBA-instance values; missing palette entries fall back to the ANSI table, missing default bg/fg to palette[0]/palette[7]); TerminalMode is the luminance rule (bg luminance > 0.5 -> 'light' else 'dark').

Theme is a resolved theme + name/mode exposing lipgloss styles (components never see hex, spec §3); fg/bg yield an empty style for an absent or transparent (alpha 0) token; SelectedForeground is the upstream contrast rule (explicit selectedListItemText wins; a transparent background contrasts via the luminance rule 0.299r+0.587g+0.114b > 0.5 -> black else white; else the background); the token accessors (Text, TextMuted, Primary, ..., Markdown*, Syntax*, Diff*) map each semantic token to a lipgloss style.

StyleConfig builds the glamour element styles from the markdown* tokens (base = 'markdownText' for text parts and 'textMuted' for reasoning, the word-wrap width also driving the horizontal-rule line length with an <4 -> 8-dash fallback); NewTranscriptRenderer builds a glamour TermRenderer word-wrapped at width, and a zero Theme (a nil-engine run) skips WithStyles so glamour renders plain with no SGR; the SGR profile is 24-bit for plain text but 256-color for the code-block path in a plain unit context, while under teatest glamour emits 256-color for both (teatest goldens pin 38;5;N); the chroma token map + the global 'charm' style-slot workaround for per-language code highlighting is the planned S1.4 work and in the current tree CodeBlock.Chroma is still nil (pinned by syntax_test.go).
